title: The half-rate linear programming bound for binary codes is $\frac12-\frac1π$
summary: In their work on sphere packing and the modular bootstrap, Afkhami-Jeddi, Cohn, Hartman, de Laat, and Tajdini conjectured the exact high-dimensional exponent of the Cohn-Elkies sphere-packing linear program. OpenAI's Chapter 1 subsequently proved their conjecture by establishing that both Fourier sign-uncertainty radii are $(1/π+o(1))\sqrt d$. We prove the binary coding analogue: \[ R_D\!\left(\frac12-\frac1π\right)=\frac12. \] We also formulate the two Krawtchouk sign-uncertainty problems and determine both of their asymptotics.
